verdict.line: You lose if you dash in while Volibear's E (Sky Splitter) is up and eat the slow into a Q stun; you win if you hold E (Slice and Dice) until his E is on cooldown, then fury-stack through him.

brief.thesis: Renekton holds the lane-advantage column but the head-to-head win rate sits flat at 49.7% over 2001 games, which tracks the fact that this is a cooldown-reading matchup, not a stat-check one. Volibear's only ranged tool is E (Sky Splitter, 16s cooldown, 1200 range) — while it's up he controls when the fight starts and gets a shield if he stands in the blast; the moment it's down, Renekton's dash range and Fury-empowered stun flip the fight one-sidedly, exactly as OP.GG's own tip describes.

theirWindow.when: His E (Sky Splitter) is up, 1200 range
theirWindow.what: He can poke and slow you from well outside your E (Slice and Dice, 450 range) threat range, then shield himself if he's standing in the blast and follow with Q (Thundering Smash) to stun your first hit. Don't walk into the bolt's landing zone or try to engage through it.

yourWindow.when: His E is down and you're above 50 Fury
yourWindow.what: Dash in with E (Slice and Dice) — empowered version also shreds his Armor — then land W (Ruthless Predator), which at 50+ Fury becomes a 3-hit stun lasting 1.5 seconds and strips any shield he's holding. Follow with Q (Cull the Meek) for the Fury-boosted heal and damage.

start.why: Picked in 72.4% of games at a 51.1% win rate over 1764 games — the extra sustain and damage matter in a lane decided by who lands the first clean trade.

boots.why: 58.1% pick rate at 49.2% win rate over 1316 games. The tenacity blunts his Q stun and R slow, both of which exist specifically to lock you down before his passive attack speed ramps.

core.why: Highest-win-rate path (55.8% over 265 games) starts here — the shield triggers exactly when you dash in with empowered E, letting you tank his W-stack trades.
Stacking armor shred compounds with your empowered E's own Armor reduction, turning your all-in window into a snowball once his E is down.
Converts his W-stack poke and Q stun damage into delayed damage you can heal through with Q (Cull the Meek) before it ever lands.

you're ahead and want to shorten your W/E cooldowns for more frequent all-ins

runes.keystoneWhy: 49.7% of games are close trades, not burst kills — Conqueror's stacking adaptive damage and self-heal on takedown reward exactly the extended, Fury-stacked fights this matchup is built around.

summoners.why: 88.2% pick rate, the standard choice here. Ignite directly answers his W (Frenzied Maul) recast heal, denying the exact sustain tool that lets him win extended trades once his passive attack speed ramps.

playing.title: Track his E, not his HP
playing.detail: Sky Splitter is a 16s cooldown with 1200 range — every all-in decision should start with whether it's up, since it's his only tool that threatens you outside dash range.

playing.title: Bank Fury before you commit
playing.detail: Both your W and Q change category entirely above 50 Fury — a 2-hit 0.75s stun becomes a 3-hit 1.5s stun that strips shields, and your Q's damage and heal both jump. Don't dash in on low Fury.

playing.title: Respect his Q speed burst
playing.detail: Thundering Smash (300 range, 12s cooldown at rank 1) gives him a gap-close plus a stun on first hit. If it's up and you're not ready to trade, don't let him get his first auto on you.

playing.title: Time E engages to his E cooldown
playing.detail: Slice and Dice at 450 range is your only way to close a gap he controls with his E. Only use it to engage when his Sky Splitter is down, otherwise you're walking into the exact poke OP.GG flags for this matchup.

playing.title: Hold W for the Fury threshold
playing.detail: If you're at 40-49 Fury, wait one more auto or Q cast before using Ruthless Predator — the gap between the 2-hit and 3-hit version is the difference between a 0.75s and a 1.5s stun, which decides whether your follow-up damage lands.

playing.title: Use your R to out-tempo his
playing.detail: Your Dominus recycles on a 120s cooldown at rank 1 versus his Stormbringer's 160s. From level 6-8 you'll have your ultimate up again before he does — look for a second all-in window he can't match.

playing.title: Buy Executioner's Calling if his sustain snowballs
playing.detail: His W2 heal and passive attack speed scaling mean a losing lane compounds fast. Grievous Wounds removes that healing entirely and should come in if you're behind on trades past level 9.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoner spells, and all win rates above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.19.1); the cooldown numbers, ability ranges, and the tactical reasoning for when to engage or hold are drawn directly from the ability text and are this brief's own analysis.
